name: pdk-jsonpath-ng-etl
instr:
We flatten package registry manifests into a TSV: for every match of `jsonpath_ng.parse('$..*').find(doc)` we write `str(match.full_path)` and the value. Later we apply a corrections file with `update` and `filter`, through those paths or selectors people type by hand, storing each selector as `str(jsonpath_ng.ext.parse(selector))`. Since we started loading the full registry dump, much of this breaks. Samples of the dump and the corrections file are in /data/registry/.

Each path we write should parse with both `jsonpath_ng.parse` and `jsonpath_ng.ext.parse` to exactly the value it came from, and print back as the same text. A stored selector should parse back to one that finds the same values and prints the same text again. Printed paths and selectors stay on one line, with no characters U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F. Paths that already parse back correctly must print exactly as today, since we join on them.

`update` through a path or selector should change exactly the values its `find` returns, and `filter` remove exactly those the function accepts.

Quoted names and strings should understand the JSON string escapes `\"`, `\\`, `\/`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and `\uXXXX` (a surrogate pair gives one character), and `\'` keeps working. A `\u` without four hex digits should raise `JsonPathLexerError`. Bare `*` and `[*]` must keep matching everything, also after printing and parsing again.

Could you find what's wrong and fix it? The existing tests in /app/tests and the mypy
